fun_highlights: The callback architecture genuinely surprises: cb_lookaway (looking away from the lonely child at age 12, then meeting a rough sleeper at age 55) and cb_books_late (the childhood book reappearing decades later) land with real emotional payoff because the connection is earned, not announced. Iris Brandt in Dynasty 1 not only chases the question but then chooses 'Look away again' at 61, which lands like a gut-punch precisely because Dynasty 1 set the memory. That kind of long-arc coherence is rare enough to feel genuinely fresh.

The vocation arcs (soldier / scholar / maker / wanderer / adrift) create structurally different lives when they actually fire in sequence. Ren Salvedi's life in Dynasty 6 — soldier, war grief, public conviction, finally reading the childhood book at 49 — reads like a complete character, not a template. The 'adrift' path is the standout: Calla Okonkwo in Dynasty 11 is one of the few lives that broke my prediction of the next beat.

Era colouring at life-opening works well. Dynasty 11's plague era reshapes the marriage framing and introduces the 'tend them, stay close' sickness card (Naima and Calla both face it), which does not appear anywhere else in the 15 dynasties. That rarity is good — it reads as historical texture, not filler.

The competing-goods cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_dream_or_duty) are the best single cards in the deck from a surprise standpoint: both options are defensible and the log line refuses to adjudicate. Annika Okonkwo's 'Held a true thing back… and was never afterward quite sure she had been right' is the kind of line that makes a player want to replay to try the other branch.

The founding-generation epitaph diversity is genuine. Across 15 dynasties: 'Gave away everything he knew, and so kept it,' 'Was poor in all but the giving of it,' 'Left before the story had found its middle,' 'Lived half in the world and half in his own head' — these do not repeat verbatim, and the themed clustering logic in dynasty.js (blocking a cluster used by the last two ancestors) demonstrably works within a single dynasty's run.

The 'five-generations' callback (Calla Brandt in Dynasty 1 gen 5, Calla Okonkwo in Dynasty 11 gen 5) where the character explicitly reckons with the founder's name — 'The founder is a stranger now. Be your own first' — is a clever generational mechanic that surprised me by arriving exactly when it should, at the right distance.
staleness: The structural spine is extremely visible across dynasties. Nearly every life runs: early-world-framing → c_origin choice → c_book or c_sibling or c_wonder → y_calling → a_marry (or a_meet_late) → a_child → vocation midlife arc → elder bequest → death. Across all 15 dynasties I could predict the category of the next beat within 2-3 events almost every time. Dynasties 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 14 are all single-generation founders whose lives compress this spine to 8-12 cards — and at that length the template is unmissable.

The 'body aging' observe() lines repeat at grinding frequency within a single long life and especially across a session. By Dynasty 6 I had already read 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them,' 'The body has begun keeping its own quiet counsel,' 'Mornings take longer to arrive in the body,' and 'The weather has begun living in his joints' so many times they had lost all weight. Dynasty 8 Cyrus (90 years) fires five body-aging observations; Dynasty 11 Yara fires four. The pool of 9-10 lines is not large enough for a 90-year life, and the vit<35 / vit<18 triggers mean every long-lived character hits both pools.

The c_move card (family packs crates, new town) fires in an implausible fraction of lives — Carys Brandt (D1 gen4 Ronja), Henrik Brandt (D1 gen3), Calla Brandt (D1 gen5), Idris Salvedi (D6 gen5), Roman Lindholm (D15). In the transcripts I counted 7 instances of 'The family packs everything it owns into crates.' The log line always says 'Grieve the one you lost' or 'Make the new place yours,' and the framing is always the same crate-packing sentence. It fires about once every 3 lives, which is too frequent for an 'once' card.

The 'mentor / teaching the young' cluster (y_mentor, m_mentor_young, e_craft, m_scholar_legacy, the bequest 'Everything I know') produces near-identical log lines in dynasty after dynasty. In Dynasty 2 Tobias says 'Gave away everything he knew, and so kept it'; in Dynasty 4 Ottilie says 'Made of her own mind a thing other people got to keep'; in Dynasty 8 Cassian says 'Left his knowing in other heads'; in Dynasty 11 Linnea says 'Taught what she knew, and so outlived the knowing of it'; in Dynasty 14 Niall says 'Poured what he knew into the young, and so refused, quietly, to die all the way.' The epitaph cluster logic blocks exact repeats within two ancestors, but the rotation across dynasties means this same cluster turns up as the closing note in roughly 1 in 3 dynasties, and the thematic similarity is visible even when the exact wording rotates.

The 'refuse a kindness repaid' (cb_outcast_return, option 'Decline. You didn't do it for this') fires in Dynasty 1 Calla (age 42), Dynasty 2 Greta (age 39), Dynasty 8 Junia (age 34), Dynasty 9 Anders (age 36), and Dynasty 11 Yara (age 43). The log line is always 'Refused to be repaid for a kindness they barely remembered giving.' This is a once-per-dynasty card but the consistent player choice toward the 'Decline' option (because it reads as the 'virtuous/interesting' option) means the line lands verbatim 5 times across 15 dynasties.

The late-life bequest card (e_bequest) fires in nearly every multi-generation dynasty and the player always sees the same four options in the same order. The log lines for 'Nothing but their own freedom' ('Decided the kindest inheritance was none at all') and 'The stories, and the warmth' ('Gave the years they had left to telling the next one exactly where they came from') appear 3+ times verbatim across the transcripts. The bequest is a strong mechanic but its prose output is too thin — one log line per choice with no variation.

improvements.what: Replace the c_move log line with a pool of at least 6-8 distinct lines, and add a cond gate so it cannot fire in consecutive generations of the same dynasty (currently only 'once' per life, not per dynasty).
improvements.why: The single 'The family packs everything it owns into crates' sentence appears verbatim 7 times across 15 dynasties. A once-per-dynasty gate and a fresh line pool would eliminate the single most repeated sentence in the entire transcript.

improvements.what: Double the observe() body-aging pools (vit_tire and vit_neg) and add a minimum-age-gap enforcement so the same line cannot fire within 8 years of a prior body observation. Currently a 90-year-old life can accumulate 5+ body observations with repeated phrases.
improvements.why: Body-observation lines are the most frequent non-choice prose in a long life. Their repetition within a single dynasty drains them of impact; by Dynasty 6 they are background noise. Larger pools + spacing enforcement would restore their ability to surprise.

improvements.what: Add prose variation to e_bequest: give each of the four choices 3-4 distinct log lines (like a_marry already does), and add at least one context-sensitive framing that reads differently if the bequest giver is a wanderer vs. a scholar vs. a maker.
improvements.why: The bequest card fires in every multi-generation dynasty and its log lines are currently single-variant. 'Decided the kindest inheritance was none at all' appears 3 times verbatim. This is the one card guaranteed to fire late in every long dynasty — it deserves the deepest prose pool in the game.

improvements.what: Add a 'third structural shape' to break the predict-the-next-category problem: introduce 2-3 cards that fire in unusual age windows or that gate on unusual combinations (e.g., a wanderer who also had a child, an adrift life that inherited wealth, a scholar who became a soldier), so at least one card per life arrives from an unexpected angle.
improvements.why: The surprise problem is architectural: the sequence of card-category is too predictable. The existing vocation arcs help but they still follow a youth→adult→midlife→elder scaffold. Cards that cross categories or fire at unexpected life-stages would introduce genuine structural unpredictability.

improvements.what: Gate the 'teaching' epitaph cluster more aggressively across dynasties — extend RECENT_CLUSTERS to block 'teacher' for 4+ recent deaths across the session, not just 3. Also add 2 new epitaph clusters for the adrift and wanderer life-shapes, which currently fall through to 'ordinary' or 'mind' more than they should.
improvements.why: The teacher/knowledge epitaph cluster dominates the session-wide epitaph distribution in the transcripts. The per-dynasty block logic works within a house but fails to prevent the cluster from dominating across houses. Adrift lives (Calla Okonkwo, Linnea Salvedi) deserve their own closing note that reads differently from 'lived half in the world and half in their own head.'

verdict: A Life has genuine craft: the callback architecture earns real emotional beats, the vocation arcs create structurally distinct lives when they fire well, and the prose quality is consistently above the genre floor. The surprise problem is structural rather than cosmetic — the card-category sequence is predictable enough that an attentive player can call the next beat type before it loads, and a handful of log lines (the crate-packing move, the body-aging observations, the 'refused to be repaid' line, the bequest prose) have been worn smooth by repetition across the 15-dynasty sample. The game is good enough to keep playing but not fresh enough to keep surprising past the fourth or fifth dynasty, which is where the 'one more life' pull stalls.
